name: Tapetum Lucidum Integration
description: Introduces a functional tapetum lucidum — the reflective layer behind the retina that gives cats their night vision and eye-shine. The modification dramatically improves low-light vision, allowing the user to see in conditions that would leave an unmodified human effectively blind. The trade-off is reduced visual acuity in bright light and the distinctive eye-shine visible when light strikes the eyes at the right angle. Combined with prismatic iris resequencing, the result is eyes that glow faintly in darkness — functional and unsettling in equal measure. Helix Biosystems' premium version includes an adaptive dimming response that reduces the bright-light penalty. Street versions lack this refinement and require tinted lenses in daylight. In the Shelf's underlevels, where reliable lighting is a luxury, tapetum integration is considered a practical necessity rather than a vanity modification.
procedure: Retinal injection under local anesthetic, single session
reversibility: Reversible with retinal resurfacing; carries risk of permanent vision reduction
side_effects: Bright light sensitivity (photophobia) in budget versions
Eyes visibly glow when light hits them — identifiable at a distance
Color perception slightly shifted toward blue-green spectrum
social_perception: Practical and common. In dark neighborhoods, it's almost standard. The eye-shine is considered attractive by many and predatory by some. Corporate security uses it as an identifier — tapetum eyes are easy to spot on camera.
story_hooks: A surveillance system identifies a suspect by their eye-shine pattern, which is as unique as a fingerprint
A batch of black-market tapetum installations causes progressive retinal degradation — the users are going blind, and the clinic has vanished
